gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many watts its top long-run pick loses at a big station's full solar-port current. The VEVOR 30 ft 10 AWG pair is a 60 ft round trip. That works out to about 0.060 Ω, so it loses about 6 W at 10 A, 24 W at 20 A, and 37.5 W at the 25 A that BLUETTI says the Elite 200 V2 accepts. No result gives cost per foot of run either: about $1.46/ft for VEVOR against $3.05/ft for EcoFlow's 2.5 m XT60i cable.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited (yourpowersetup.com and stormwatts.com/solar-panel-compatibility) and two uncited top results (ridgewatt.com/learn/solar-cables, powerstationtips.com/mc4-to-xt60-adapter-guide). The two cited pages give no gauge, loss or length figures at all. Ridgewatt already has a percent-loss table for 25 ft and 50 ft at 10, 12 and 14 AWG, but only for one 200 W panel at 9.9 A. Powerstationtips gives drop percentages at 6 A and 16–17 A. No page works out the loss for the specific cables ChatGPT showed, the loss at a 20–25 A port maximum, or price per foot of run. The loss method itself is not new, which is why this scores 1.
decides: It confirms 10 AWG for long runs only when the current is high. At the 10 A a single 200 W panel delivers, the 30 ft VEVOR pair loses about 6 W, roughly 3%. At 20–25 A into an Elite 200 V2 class station it loses 24–37.5 W. The same run in 12 AWG would lose about 38 W at 20 A. For short leads, gauge barely matters and the connector decides the pick. EcoFlow's US store sells the XT60i version at 2.5 m, not the 3.5 m ChatGPT showed. The 3.5 m length is the older XT60 version. EcoFlow also lists a separate XT60i-to-LP60 cable for the DELTA Gen4 solar input, so the cable ChatGPT showed is not a direct fit for that newest line.
